title: What would actually make AI prototyping useful instead of just another toy?
author: puchi_mentos
selftext:
I’ve been trying to do more game idea testing with AI, mostly to move faster in the early stages.

The thing I keep wanting is a tool that can fully do iteration for me. It's such a slow process, and I need something that gives me 5 different variations from a game mechanic or idea I described. Then I could pick the most promising one, tweak it, generate another round, and test from there.

Curious what you think about a tool like that. Maybe there is a tool that does this already?

What features should it have to not just be another AI toy, but to actually help with real games? 

Also curious how people are currently testing early game ideas. Do you usually build one rough prototype, make several variants manually, test, and ship, or something else?

I just really hate the iteration part and want to make it easier lol :D

comments.author: Casiper
comments.body: Planning before creating is what I do. 😹

replies.author: puchi_mentos
replies.body: well you can plan and plan, but it's still not gonna be the same when you start building and iterating imo

comments.author: ffxivthrowaway03
comments.body:
If your separation from "it's a toy" to "its a productivity tool" is that you literally want to just go "make me five similar games!" and have it do *all of that* instantly... your definitions are the problem.  I've used AI for ideation, feature and genre trend research, UI/UX design, implementation, art direction... you name it and AI can help with it if you leverage it correctly.  That's not "just a toy" at all, that's real work being done.  

If you wan to just type "make gaem nao" into a prompt and have it do literally everything in AAA studio quality, you're always going to be disappointed.  Realign your expectations.

replies.author: puchi_mentos
replies.body: I make very simple games that have a lot of repetition and iteration. The game gen ai tools that I've used all feel like they promise a lot and can't deliver. I'm not saying what you mentioned is not work, it's just not a relevant part for me. I'm looking for something that can make versions fast so I can test and save time iterating .

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body:
Then maybe you should clearly define what you're trying to accomplish instead of writing off the whole technology sector as "just toys."

But it sounds more like you're looking to automate the already saturated shovelware slop market to make a quick buck to me.  I'm not sure you're gonna find a receptive audience for helping with that.

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body: I do ai tdd. I have hade great successes but limited time spent. So nothing real to show yet.

comments.author: DatabaseConstant7870
comments.body: I’m on version 3 rn of my game, first I started in threejs, got it to a place where my homies could test it and even load into the same game as me. One of my homies is into the style of game and he got pretty hooked for a good 3 hours, that told me I was on the right track. I then started a new version with c++ and raylib, this one felt really great the movement was faster it used my gpu and cpu making the fps go hundreds of fps above my cap, it’s at a nice place for now. Version 3 is also in raylib but this time I’ve learned how to give cursor skills to use when being given certain tasks so I gave it skills to build from modular asset packs for houses and buildings, I got it to load in a modular character pack, and have the game loop working but the game loop is different from the first two and I think after I get this to where I like it I will take the game loop from the first two versions and mix that with the work flow I had on this third version to really create a great game with modular assets and a fun game loop

replies.author: puchi_mentos
replies.body: thats still quite a lot of manual work. is it not annoying to rebuild each time?

replies.author: DatabaseConstant7870
replies.body: From someone who started learning how to code and use things like unity and unreal 14 years ago when I was in highschool, ai can be a really fun tool but if it’s just streamlining everything it’s going to miss stuff in all builds it makes, this will then eat more tokens, cause the user to go with something they didn’t initially want. If ai is going to be used it’s important humans utilize their ideas not the AIs, there’s too much slop out there, too many tools making slop, too many people thinking a top down shooter with neon colors is the next cod arcade zombies. The tokens it would use up are yours not the consumer so then you have to pay business prices for business style accounts. Theres a lot that would have to go into this and if you aren’t the creator of a tool like revolt then your leagues behind a lot of people. You could try hitting people up who have made tools that are like that, figure out their business models, how they figure out pricing for tokens, and the conversion of their tokens to the ai model their using tokens. How much you’ll take from the top, what skills to give the ai model your having run this whole system. This sounds more like a slop machine as of right now

comments.author: North-Tie-2364
comments.body: Using AI is not different from regular product development cycles with a team. You need a plan and you need a ton of documentation. As you build, you need to log what you built, what it does, what systems it connects to, and when you reference that in the future, you need to load that documentation into the context window. Having a clear plan and clean documentation will save you a ton of rebuild time.

comments.author: table_dropper
comments.body:
Figure out which tasks you keep repeating, then automate those tasks. AI can take care of some of it, but to get a game working and feeling good, it requires a human to test it out. Whats sped up the testing process is to create individual test levels for each major feature. The level has floating text with debug logs and values as well as testing instructions. If something doesnt work correctly, i can give the values to the ai with whats off and iterate that way. 

The next thing I'll be trying is adding MCPs to allow agents to play the game, but I'm not sure it's at the point where an MCP would really accelerate anything.
